correctness.rationale: At scale three the twelve vertices are the even-sign signed permutations of (3,1,1), and the tetrahedron-edge subdivisions and four triangular truncation faces give 18 edges, every endpoint dot product 7 and squared norm 11. All generic section vertices are transverse crossings of edges; vertex-incident normals form a null union of great circles. Even-sign symmetry of the solid plus reversal of the central-plane normal reduces the area calculation to x>y>z>0, of area π/12. In (y/x,z/x), the four possible sign changes give exactly the six listed regions. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 2` builds all rational ray intersections from vertex normals and cone boundaries, tests every vertex sign assignment for interior, and counts crossings at a rational interior ray using the nearest-pair graph. It finds exactly those six regions, two for each count, and sums chamber solid angles to 0.21593608531264044, 0.5202474652389364, 0.26381644944842314. For the two four-section triangles the absolute ray determinants are 2 and 1, and their dot-product and norm denominators are the exact D₁ and D₂ in the finding. The probability an edge with endpoint angle arccos(7/11) is separated by the central plane is that angle divided by π, so the mean is exactly m; on {4,5,6}, the total mass and mean then fix the other two atoms. The finite chamber enumeration checks the whole generic sign arrangement, not a sample of orientations. The frozen verification and checker were inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The distinct same-day published Haar polygon law has literally the same scaled solid, central sampling and counted statistic, supplies the entire law, and also resolves the finer full great-circle chamber structure. The exact arctan and arccos forms can be identified geometrically, not just by matching decimals. Let Ω₁ and Ω₂ be the frozen four-section triangle areas with ray determinants 2 and 1. Reflect the first triangle across y=z to make an unsplit spherical quadrilateral. The two opposite corners away from the mirror have angle θ₁=arccos(1/11); the mirror corners have angles θ₅ and π−θ₇ from their vertex-normal dot products. Spherical excess gives 2Ω₁=−π+2θ₁+θ₅−θ₇. The second triangle is one eighth of the axial octagon x≥max(3|y|+|z|,|y|+3|z|); its four corners with one of y,z zero have angle π−θ₉ and the four equal-absolute-coordinate corners have angle π−θ₇. Thus 8Ω₂=2π−4θ₇−4θ₉. The overlap source sums these shapes with multiplicities 24 and 6, giving exactly 48(Ω₁+Ω₂)/(4π)=q, and the identical mean fixes the other probabilities. No priority inference follows from the common catalogue day.
